name: Stiff Little Fingers
label: Rough Trade
lede: Four Belfast schoolboys swapped Deep Purple covers for songs about the Troubles, packaged their first single like a bomb, and made the first independent album to reach the UK Top 20.

eras.title: Highway Star finds punk
eras.text: Jake Burns, Henry Cluney and Brian Faloon started out at Belfast Boys' Model School playing rock covers. Punk arrived, a journalist brought a friend to a hotel gig, and the band started writing about the city they lived in.

years.cap: Snapshot and ticket for a Stiff Little Fingers show, December 14, 1977
years.src: Wikipedia: Stiff Little Fingers · Perfect Sound Forever: Henry Cluney (2021) · Guitar World
years.h: Highway Star becomes Stiff Little Fingers, by way of the Fast
years.p: Bassist Gordon Blair leaves for Rudi and [[Ali McMordie|486776ba-6487-4814-8173-1cbf8a302e61]] takes over. Cluney, the glam fan who'd found punk first, gets the band off Deep Purple; the new name comes from a Vibrators song on Pure Mania.
years.xp:
The covers band had been named after Deep Purple's Highway Star, Burns's pick. Cluney told Perfect Sound Forever that Burns taught him guitar at school, and that his own first concert was Rory Gallagher at the Ulster Hall in January 1975.

Burns had his own Gallagher story: at about 11 he saw a Taste farewell concert on Northern Ireland TV. "This noise came from the TV, and it transfixed me," he told Guitar World.

years.src: Wikipedia: Stiff Little Fingers · Perfect Sound Forever: Henry Cluney (2021) · Guitar World
years.h: A night at the Glenmachan Hotel brings in Gordon Ogilvie
years.p: Journalist Colin McClelland brings his friend Gordon Ogilvie to a gig at the Glenmachan Hotel, Belfast. Ogilvie pushes the band to write about growing up in the Troubles, and the two become its managers.
years.xp: Ogilvie co-wrote much of the early material. Cluney: "Gordon wrote most of the lyrics. He was great with words." Burns has always pushed back on the press calling Ogilvie a Svengali, telling Guitar World that sometimes Ogilvie gave him one line, as with Alternative Ulster, and sometimes far more.

eras.title: A single that looked like a bomb
eras.text: In one year the band went from a jingle studio at a Belfast radio station to John Peel's show, a Rough Trade deal and a support slot with the Tom Robinson Band. Island Records nearly signed them, then didn't.

years.cap: Stiff Little Fingers under a Danger Keep Out sign, Belfast, c. 1978
years.h: 'Suspect Device' gets its first airing at the Pound Club, with Ulster TV filming
years.p: The first live performance of 'Suspect Device' is filmed for 'It Makes You Want to Spit', Ulster Television's programme on Belfast punk, broadcast on March 6.

years.cap: The cassette-bomb fold-out sleeve of 'Suspect Device', Rigid Digits, 1978
years.src: Wikipedia: Stiff Little Fingers · Perfect Sound Forever: Henry Cluney (2023)
years.h: A record company drops 'Suspect Device' in a bucket of water
years.p: Recorded in a radio-station studio built for jingles and issued on the band's own Rigid Digits label, the debut single comes in a sleeve made to look like a cassette incendiary device. One label phoned for another copy: they'd soaked the first in case it was real.
years.xp:
Ogilvie wrote the words; Burns put a tune to them, and wrote 'Wasted Life' around the same time. McClelland got them the studio time at the local radio station.

Cluney's own verdict on where the riff came from, to Perfect Sound Forever: "'Suspect Device' IS 'Space Station #5.' Shhhhhh."

years.src: Wikipedia: Stiff Little Fingers · Dying Scene (2019)
years.h: John Peel keeps playing it, and Rough Trade calls
years.p: A copy reaches [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]], who plays it again and again. [[Rough Trade|4f4b0013-1704-4936-a769-e6e8a6e08ff8]] takes on distribution, re-presses the single a month later, and it sells over 30,000; the band's first Peel session airs April 13.
years.xp: Burns called Peel's backing "like being anointed by the powers that be" in a 2019 Dying Scene interview. By the end of the year Peel's listeners had voted 'Suspect Device' No. 4 and 'Alternative Ulster' No. 11 in the Festive Fifty.

years.cap: Stiff Little Fingers on the cover of In the City fanzine
years.src: Wikipedia: Stiff Little Fingers · Guitar World
years.h: 'Alternative Ulster' was meant to be a free fanzine flexi
years.p: Written to be given away with the fanzine of the same name, the song came out as the second single on Rough Trade instead. The recording began life as a demo for Island Records, produced by Ed Hollis.
years.xp:
Burns played it to the writer Gavin Martin first. Martin, Burns told Guitar World, "said he thought it was shit."

Hollis asked for the guitars to be doubled. With no click track or count-in, Burns had to guess where the first guitar came in, and it took forever.

years.h: Island signs them, then the deal falls through
years.p: The band had a contract with Island Records for the album; it collapsed, so the record went to Rough Trade, the label already selling their singles. They spent the second half of the year opening for the Tom Robinson Band.

eras.title: Number 14, on an independent
eras.text: Inflammable Material took a Rough Trade record into the Top 20. The year also moved the band to London, cost them their drummer, and put them at the top of the bill at the Ulster Hall.

years.src: Wikipedia: Inflammable Material · Guitar World · Wikipedia: Stiff Little Fingers
years.h: Inflammable Material is the first indie album in the UK Top 20
years.p: Cut in under two weeks at Spaceward Studios, Cambridge, with Rough Trade's [[Geoff Travis|70437714-3183-4916-947f-e5ba2154d16a]] and [[Mayo Thompson|b463f760-e381-462a-b060-78606b78e5e1]] producing, it reaches No. 14 and sells over 100,000 copies. Paul Morley calls it the classic punk rock record in NME.
years.xp:
"We literally went into the studio and recorded our live set," Burns told Guitar World. Nobody owned a tuner: "We just tuned to whoever's guitar sounded most in tune. That's how green we were in the studio!" Of the producers he said nobody knew what they were doing, "the blind leading the blind," and that made it exciting.

It gets called "the Irish record," but Burns counts only about four of the 13 songs as specifically about Northern Ireland. 'Johnny Was' is a Bob Marley song moved to Belfast.

q: A great record, although at the time we weren't impressed.
years.h: The Undertones say SLF sensationalise the Troubles
years.p: Derry's The Undertones accused the band of cashing in on the conflict; Stiff Little Fingers said the Undertones ignored it. Undertones bassist Michael Bradley later admitted some of it was jealousy.
years.xp: Bradley's memoir describes John O'Neill laying into Burns verbally in 1979, slagging his records and the journalist writing the songs. Good Vibrations boss Terri Hooley called SLF "the ones that got away" and said his own sniping was probably jealousy.

years.src: Wikipedia: Stiff Little Fingers · Perfect Sound Forever: Henry Cluney (2021)
years.h: Brian Faloon stays in Belfast; Jim Reilly answers an ad
years.p: The move to London costs the band drummer Faloon and co-manager Colin McClelland. Reilly, also from Belfast, arrives in time for the 'Gotta Gettaway' single and the Rock Against Racism tour.
years.xp: Cluney told Perfect Sound Forever that Faloon left after a girlfriend's ultimatum, and that his own favourite record was Go for It: "The lineup with Jim had energy and an edge."

years.h: The first local punk band to headline the Ulster Hall sells it out
years.p: The 21-date 'Gotta Gettaway' tour, their first as headliners, comes home to the biggest venue in Belfast. Reilly said the room held kids from both sides of a city still at war.
years.xp: Reilly's memory of the night: a packed hall of young people having a great time, and the sense that the band was doing "something that none of the politicians were able to do," bringing the city together regardless of religion.

years.h: Rigid Digits moves to Chrysalis
years.p: The band takes its own label to Chrysalis Records, so Inflammable Material stays their only Rough Trade album.

eras.title: Top of the Pops, then fistfights
eras.text: Chrysalis put the band on Top of the Pops and Go for It back at No. 14. By 1983 the songs were darker, the crowds smaller, and the members were settling arguments with their fists.

years.cap: Stiff Little Fingers on Rockpalast, Germany, 1980
years.src: SLF official site · Wikipedia: Stiff Little Fingers
years.h: Nobody's Heroes, made with a deadline for the first time
years.p: The second album, and the first on Chrysalis. Burns, looking back for its 2026 reissue, said they were suddenly under pressure, which had never been the case before.

yt: 'At the Edge', Top of the Pops, February 15, 1980
years.h: Miming 'At the Edge' gets them a warning from Top of the Pops
years.p: The band mimes 'At the Edge' on BBC One and is told it didn't take the show seriously enough to come back. It comes back anyway, for 'Nobody's Hero' in May and 'Just Fade Away' in 1981.

years.cap: Poster for Stiff Little Fingers at the Apollo, Glasgow, May 24, 1981
years.h: Go for It takes on domestic abuse and football violence
years.p: Recorded in two weeks at Jam Studios, Finsbury Park, with Doug Bennett, the third studio album hits No. 14. 'Hits and Misses' is about domestic abuse; Trouser Press heard a smoother, less anguished Burns.

years.h: Burns makes his acting debut in a BBC Play for Today
years.p: He appears in Iris in the Traffic, Ruby in the Rain, written by Belfast playwright Stewart Parker.

years.src: Wikipedia: Stiff Little Fingers · Perfect Sound Forever: Henry Cluney (2023)
years.h: Dolphin Taylor of the Tom Robinson Band takes over the drums
years.p: Go for It is Reilly's last record with the band. Reilly and Cluney later play together again in XSLF.

years.h: Now Then..., the one Burns rated highest
years.p: The fourth studio album follows the four-song EP £1.10 or Less. It is Taylor's first album with the band, and the sales and crowds are shrinking.

years.big: "The best I think we will ever make."
q: Couldn't stand the sight of each other.
years.h: Burns calls it a day
years.p: Burns said Now Then... was their best record and the best they would make, so he was ending the band. The members later admitted they'd been having fistfights rather than talking.

eras.title: The temporary reunion that stuck
eras.text: A reunion tour meant to be a one-off sold out night after night, so the band kept going. Over the next two decades a bassist from the Jam came and went, a founder was let go by phone, and Burns moved to Chicago.

years.src: Wikipedia: Stiff Little Fingers · Wikipedia: Jake Burns
years.h: Critics say nobody will come; the German shows sell out
years.p: Burns had spent the gap with Jake Burns and the Big Wheel, with drummer Steve Grantley. The re-formed band tours with shows selling out night after night, and the temporary reunion becomes permanent.

years.src: Wikipedia: Stiff Little Fingers · Wikipedia: Jake Burns
years.h: Bruce Foxton of the Jam replaces Ali McMordie
years.p: McMordie can't commit to full-time touring. [[Bruce Foxton|18f3b19a-eeee-4c02-a856-0a4639a693dd]], who had demoed songs with Burns after the 1983 split, plays bass on Flags and Emblems.

years.h: 'Beirut Moon' is pulled on its day of release
years.p: The Flags and Emblems single is withdrawn from sale in Britain on day one, reportedly because it criticised the government over the hostage John McCarthy, held in Lebanon.

years.src: Perfect Sound Forever: Henry Cluney (2023) · Wikipedia: Stiff Little Fingers
years.h: The manager phones Henry Cluney to say he's out
years.p: Cluney, who named the band, is asked to leave. Burns, Foxton and Taylor carry on with [[Ian McCallum|4d110b57-1539-40e6-bf5c-61b1aa68fe72]] or Dave Sharp on second guitar.
years.xp: Cluney has never accepted the word "left." He told Perfect Sound Forever in 2023 that the others "did the cowardly thing and had the manager...call me and tell me my services were no longer required." He went on to form XSLF with Jim Reilly.

years.h: Steve Grantley comes over from the Big Wheel
years.p: Taylor leaves for family reasons. Grantley, Burns's drummer in the late 1980s, plays on Tinderbox (1997), and McCallum is a full member by Hope Street (1999).

years.h: Foxton leaves after fifteen years, and McMordie walks back in
years.p: Five days after Foxton's exit, the original bassist is announced for the March tour. Burns tells the message board McMordie will stay as long as his schedule allows.

eras.title: Funded in five hours
eras.text: Fans paid for the tenth album before a note was released. Ten years later Burns's knees took the band off the American road, while the Rough Trade records got the deluxe treatment.

years.h: Fans fund No Going Back in five hours
years.p: The PledgeMusic campaign launched in October 2013 hits its target in five hours. The album is the band's first No. 1 on the BBC Rock Album Chart.

years.cap: McMordie, Burns and McCallum in Chicago
years.src: Wikipedia: Stiff Little Fingers · Dying Scene (2019) · Wikipedia: Jake Burns
years.h: Thirty-seven years in, a US tour with Bad Religion and the Offspring
years.p: Stiff Little Fingers join the Summer Nationals with [[The Offspring|23a03e33-a603-404e-bcbf-2c00159d7067]], [[Bad Religion|149e6720-4e4a-41a4-afca-6d29083fc091]], [[Pennywise|5c210861-2ce2-4be3-9307-bbcfc361cc01]], [[The Vandals|f54fc7c3-3a40-4f26-83cf-328d9b097e93]] and [[Naked Raygun|85d2e30c-92fd-4c7f-a2dc-f988a70e234d]]. Burns has lived in Chicago since 2004.
years.xp: Burns moved to Chicago to marry and found it a lot like Belfast, "working class, blue collar," he told Dying Scene. He later became a US citizen, partly, he said, to help vote out Donald Trump.

years.h: The last full US tour starts in Boston
years.p: Twenty-seven dates, ending at Punk Rock Bowling in Las Vegas on May 27. Burns told Dying Scene his knees pretty much made the decision for him.
years.xp: He didn't want to be one of those bands easing off in their sixties, he said, and would rather tour less than tour worse.

years.h: Inflammable Material comes back as a 4CD/DVD box
years.p: The Rough Trade debut is reissued on 2LP, 2CD and a 4CD/DVD set with unreleased demos, live recordings and BBC sessions. A remastered Nobody's Heroes follows in September 2026.
